mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 6-month average predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs eroding equity valuation multiples.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 6-month moving average by at least 0.25 percentage points and persists for ≥2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS spike period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS relative to INDPRO indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS / INDPRO > 1.02 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with PAYEMS/INDPRO ratio improvement (Pearson ρ < 0.1, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST above the 12-month rolling average suggests growing industrial production momentum, which elevates earnings growth expectations and supports positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 50 non-overlapping 20-day windows with HOUST > 12-month avg, SPX 20d returns are negative on average (mean < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO accompanied by elevated GDPC1 (real GDP) suggests supply-side weakness, which typically precedes equity market compression and negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 2% while GDPC1 rises > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: During such INDPRO/GDPC1 cross-signal events, 20d forward returns are not significantly negative (median ≤ 0, one-sided t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the expectation of lower labor-cost pressures prompts risk-on sentiment, producing positive S&P 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during UNRATE < 4.0 periods are not statistically higher than baseline (mean diff ≤ 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in RSAFS (retail sales) above the prior 4-week average, without a corresponding rise in PAYEMS, signals demand-side strength without labor cost pressures, forecasting positive S&P 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 4-week moving average by ≥ 2% while PAYEMS remains flat for ≥1 month
failure_condition: During qualifying RSAFS/PAYEMS events, 20d forward returns are not significantly positive (median ≤ 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of CPIAUCSL inflation above 2% combined with falling INDPRO suggest persistent cost-push pressures that depress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 2.0 for two consecutive months AND INDPRO < 105.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such cross-signal periods, 20d forward returns are not statistically negative (median ≥ 0, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in UNRATE accompanied by a steady FEDFUNDS rate below 4% creates a risk-off environment where S&P 60-day forward returns are expected to trend negative due to lower growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0 for 4 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 4.0 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 10 such 60-day windows, 60d forward returns are not consistently negative (median ≥ 0.01, p > 0.05).
